title: Identification of a highly specific chymase as the major angiotensin II-forming enzyme in the human heart
authors: Urata H, Kinoshita A, Misono KS, Bumpus FM, Husain A
population: Enzyme purified from human left ventricular cardiac membranes
funder: not read: the publisher page is not accessible and the PubMed abstract carries no funding statement.
result: Angiotensin II-forming activity in human left ventricle is minimally inhibited by ACE inhibitors, and over 75% is inhibited by serine proteinase inhibitors. The major activity was purified 115,150-fold as a 30 kDa chymotrypsin-like serine proteinase of the chymase subfamily, highly specific for converting angiotensin I to angiotensin II plus His-Leu (kcat/Km 198 per min per µM); it did not degrade angiotensin II or bradykinin and did not form angiotensin II from angiotensinogen.
